key_insight: Water vapor retards grain growth and sintering in yttria-stabilized zirconia, potentially through OH-mediated grain-boundary stabilization and oxygen-vacancy depletion.
engineering_relevance: Steam exposure may help YSZ thermal barrier coatings retain porosity and limit thermal-conductivity increases during high-temperature service.
method: Heat-treated YSZ pellets with three initial porosities and free-standing plasma-sprayed coatings at 1300 °C.
Compared dry air, steam, and dry nitrogen to isolate water-vapor effects.
Used DFT and defect-equilibrium sensitivity analysis to investigate the proposed mechanism.
evidence_signal: After 100 h, the most porous pellet had 31% smaller grains in steam, with apparent rate constants 2.8–4.2 times lower; coatings retained higher porosity and showed lower thermal conductivity at intermediate exposures.
watch_item: Results from pellets and free-standing coatings at 1300 °C do not establish durability benefits for bonded coatings under thermal cycling.
paper_title: Water vapor retards grain growth during sintering of yttria-stabilized zirconia pellets and coatings
